newsitem.title: FRANCE: Doctor to pay damages to Mitterrand's kin over book.
newsitem.headline: Doctor to pay damages to Mitterrand's kin over book.

text.p: A court on Wednesday ordered Francois Mitterrand's doctor to pay damages to the late French president's relatives, and upheld a ban on the book disclosing details of his fatal cancer.

Dr Claude Gubler had already been sentenced to a four-month suspended jail term for breaching medical secrecy by revealing in a book that Mitterrand misled the French people for over a decade about the illness which finally killed him.

The court which heard the case on Wednesday ruled that Gubler should pay 340,000 francs ($68,000) to Mitterrand's relatives for invasion of privacy in his book Le Grand Secret (The Big Secret). The family had asked for 800,000 francs ($160,000).
Published a week after Mitterrand died in January, and eight months after he left office, the book was banned within 24 hours after its first print run of 40,000 copies had sold out.
In the book, Gubler revealed that Mitterrand, a Socialist who served two seven-year terms beginning in 1981, learned he had cancer within months of his election but kept it secret until 1992.
Despite a pledge of openness about his health, Mitterrand issued misleading medical bulletins twice a year.

The physician testified that he wrote to set the record straight rather than for personal gain and pledged to donate any proceeds to charity after payment of his legal bills. He no longer practises medicine.

Gubler said he agreed to keep the cancer from the public -- and not to resign as the president's physician -- because he felt that Mitterrand had trapped him into lying by ordering him to treat the illness as a state secret.
The book provides painful details about Mitterrand's diagnoses and treatments as well as the president's anxieties and argued that he was unfit to rule by November 1994.
